Kamin-Kashyrskyy Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volyn Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Kamin-Kashyrskyy's Jewish community was first recorded in the mid-16th century, growing to 1,189 (98 percent of the population) by 1897 and including Trysk and Kobrin Hasids. A self-defense group formed in 1918 helped prevent two pogrom attempts, though 120 Jews were still murdered in 1920. In May 1942, a ghetto here held 3,000 Jews from the town and surrounding villages; on August 10, 1942, 1,700 were murdered directly at this cemetery. More than 600 Jewish workers remained until November 2, 1942, when around 400 attempted to escape — only 100 survived, joining the partisans. Monuments were erected at the ghetto site and two execution sites in 1992.
